chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The most beloved of the dyes to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was the vinegar.

key_terms.الْأَصْبَاغِ: Dyes/Condiments (plural of صَبْغ, often used for vinegar in this context)

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's favorite food or condiment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) stating that vinegar (al-khal) was the most beloved dye to the Prophet (SAW), a term often interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to its use in preserving food or its distinct color. This tradition underscores the Prophetic emphasis on simple, healthful sustenance and is frequently cited in medical hadiths for vinegar's therapeutic properties. The preference highlights the Islamic value of moderation and the spiritual cleanliness associated with basic, unadulterated foods.
